Clinical trials
How can I find an ongoing clinical trial?
Via the search button, you can perform a targeted search for canine clinical trials. In order to do this, tick -if known- the box of your dog’s tumour type (‘Select tumour type’) and/or the countries (‘Select location’) for which you wish to know whether clinical trials are ongoing.
Afterwards, a list of trials for which your dog might be eligible will appear. The listed information is limited to
Treatment centre where the trial is available
In/exclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria describe the criteria necessary for your dog to participate in the trial (e.g. inoperable tumour). Exclusion criteria describe conditions that exclude possible participation to the trial (e.g. concomitant chemotherapy).
Contact information: phone number and e-mail address of the trial’s contact person,  webpage with more information on the trial.
For more details on the trial, we recommend you to contact the researchers via the listed contact info.

Cardiac ultrasound to explore the effects of chemotherapy on the heart (diagnostic trial)
All tumour types
Inclusion criteria:
Dogs diagnosed with any type of cancer that will receive doxorubicin-based therapy (e.g. CHOP, doxorubicine monotherapy, doxorubicine combi with carboplatin, ...) in consultation with a veterinary oncologist.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients receiving positive inotropic drugs, such as pimobendan, digoxin, theophylline, catecholamines...
Patients that have had any type of chemotherapy (e.g. Palladia, …) before the inclusion to the study  (prednisolone is allowed) (exception can be made for CHOP protocol - please contact study investigators)
Patients with systemic hypertension or patients receiving medication to control this (e.g. ACEi, telmisartan, amlodipine…)
Patients with hypothyroidism (will not standardly be tested before inclusion, only when clinically suspected)
Patients with chronic kidney disease
Patients with clinically significant echocardiographic abnormalities at the beginning of the study
